title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-25
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. West's lead has found South's weak suit. There are only 5 top tricks (2 spades, the ♥A, the ♦A, and the ♣A). It appears that the contract will depend on the position of the ♦K.

South can succeed some of the time that East has the ♦K by playing clubs first. The opening lead should be won in dummy so that a club can be played towards the closed hand. If East has both the ♣K and ♣Q, the contract is certain. If East splits his honours, South can win the ♣A and develop 4 more club tricks. If East follows low, South can take a winning finesse and switch his attack to diamonds, again making at least 9 tricks.

If West is able to win the club trick, he will continue spades to South's ♠K. South can now cash the ♣A. If the other club honour drops, South will have at least 9 tricks. If the clubs are not good, South will have to depend on the diamond finesse.
